summary.intent: Evaluate how well the wisp plugins served front-end work and design ideation across the orin-dx and pages projects, then act on the findings by building a lighter v5 plugin set, resolving review findings, and trimming over-engineered tests and hooks.
summary.outcome: Analysis showed the spec-driven plugins were too rigid for exploratory design work and had no visual capability. A v5 (wisp core, wisp-packs, trimmed muse and courier) was merged on v5-core and pushed as Entire trail #414. Three review findings were fixed and resolved, live smoke tests passed, and the over-built tests and Stop hook fingerprint were trimmed and committed, but the trim was not yet pushed.

repo: The old plugins formed a spec-driven lifecycle with typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas and default-fail gates; no plugin has any browser, screenshot, visual or generative mode.
muse docs reference a ranger accessibility taxonomy that was never implemented, so implemented a11y was never checked.
spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints, visual references or copy, so a spec can pass the gate while saying nothing about appearance.

Across about 810 session files only 2 top-level orin-dx sessions and 1 pages session used plugin agents; most files were subagent transcripts. All design ideation ran through Artifacts, forks, general-purpose agents and local dev servers.

The muse exit-gate caught real cross-spec contradictions and contrast failures (e.g. 2.82:1), but many late blockers were wording churn; it escalated after 3 retries and the orchestrator carried on anyway.
Visual defects (NavSheet not full screen, translucency, touch target size) were found only by the user's eye after specs passed the gate; stale numeric values in specs also drifted from the code.
In plugin hooks, Claude Code slash-command arguments work and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is substituted, but non-interactive -p mode needs `allowed-tools: Read` in skill frontmatter.

Merging the v5 branches conflicted in harnesses/codex/catalog.json, marketplace.json and .claude-plugin/marketplace.json; generated Codex files are fixed by regenerating with `just marketplace-sync` and `just claude-manifests-sync` rather than hand edits.

The three findings on change #6 were real bugs: pack-inject closed a fence on any shorter marker, stop-check joined repo-root-relative git paths to a subdirectory cwd, and release.py could reuse a stale local tag and publish an older commit.

Tests split into real-code tests (hooks, release, sync, Codex builder), which caught real bugs, and prose wording pins, which broke on every refactor and were deleted (221 to 168 tests, 27 to 19 files).

code.finding: The fingerprint/state-dir rule I added beyond the spec caused the subdirectory bug and was removed; the hook now blocks once on a dirty tree without a `Not verified:` line, with stop_hook_active ending the loop.
Fence parsing now closes only on a matching marker of at least the opening length, so a four-backtick Markdown example no longer activates a pack.
Release now refuses unpushed local tags pointing at an older commit than HEAD, preventing a resumed release from publishing stale code.

workflow: Passing hypotheses to running subagents with SendMessage let the user's rigidity lens be tested against transcript evidence, and it was strongly supported, including by the user's own 14 Oct statement.
Subagent reports and sweep results were re-verified (re-grep, rerun `just check`) before committing; a sweep introduced stale muse:component references that a first-pass grep missed.
Commit fixes and push before marking findings resolved, so the resolution references the pushed commit.
Live `claude -p --plugin-dir` smoke tests on a throwaway fixture repo are a cheap way to validate plugin flows beyond unit tests.
Test counts and kinds should be audited: tests that pin prose wording cost more than they give, while tests of executable code earn their keep.

friction: Agents stalled on 60-130 KB spec and plan files, with 17 failed agent tasks and 32 stalled mentions.
The orchestrator ignored the gate's escalate-to-human rule and made design calls itself, and the user had to repeatedly ask to be shown visuals instead of text.
Cross-session design decisions were lost, e.g. the page-width decision, which frustrated the user.
An initial session count was wrong: the corpus held a few real sessions and the rest were subagent transcripts.
A merge edit deleted one line too many and broke marketplace.json, requiring a fix.
The classifier denied deleting merged remote branches and resolving Entire findings on trail #386.
The first sweep left retired-pipeline constitution rules and introduced stale muse:component references, needing a second pass.
open_items: Merge trail #414 (needs review and merge queue), then run `just release` for 5.0.0; push the trim commit onto v5-core first.
Retry the denied cleanups: delete merged remote branches and resolve three Entire findings on trail #386.
Prepare PRs for Callisto, Caliper, Monokl and Pages to switch to wisp, courier, muse and wisp-packs with Packs: lines, held until #414 merges.
The Stop hook's block path has only unit-test coverage; the smoke tests did not exercise it.
The muse sketch/promote and exploratory path is untested in real design work; whether v5 lowers gate rounds, turns or tokens is unmeasured.
Pack taste calls are pending: expect/panic, camino and FxHashMap, never any/unknown in TS, and a third house pack for cross-language writing rules.
The UI pack waits on the brand source of truth.
Antigravity pack delivery is unverified, and Codex has no session-start injection.
Whether the new tests fail without their fixes was not checked.
